terminal: make type-ahead local echo agree with shell output

Local echo (type-ahead) shows predicted keystrokes before the shell echoes them. When a prediction
was wrong, or when the echo did not use the expected form, the terminal could show text that did
not agree with the shell. This change makes the displayed result always agree with the shell
output, and adds support for more shells.

- Make sure that the rollback of a prediction restores the authoritative cells, colors, attributes,
  cursor position, and cursor visibility. This includes styled blanks, wide cells, scroll, wrap, and
  queued output that xterm did not parse yet.
- Calculate the restore sequence after each predicted character from the parsed pen. Remove the
  SGR tracking that became incorrect after a cursor restore (ESC 8, CSI ?1049l).
- Parse escape sequences across output chunks, so that split control strings do not break the match.
- Do not make predictions in insert mode or when auto-wrap is off.
- Do not hold a typed space after a deferred wrap.
- Add support for line repaints from fish (autosuggestions, recolor, erase to end of line,
  mid-line backspace) and from PSReadLine in PowerShell (full-line repaints with absolute cursor
  position).
- Add a deterministic differential fuzzer. It compares a terminal that uses type-ahead with a
  control terminal that does not, for bash/zsh, extended edits and modes, line wrap, fish, and
  PowerShell profiles. Failures show the seed and a replay trace.
- Add regression tests that use echo sequences captured from bash, zsh, fish 4, and pwsh 7.

Validation:
- ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/typeAhead/test/browser/terminalTypeAhead.test.ts --disable-gpu: 400 passing
- Fuzzer stress run with 256 steps for each seed and profile: passing
- pnpm run typecheck-client: passing
- pnpm run eslint on the changed files: passing

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/126209

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The retention, suppression, timeout reset, and full join are directly traced in changed code. Large chunked terminal control payloads are realistic, though their prevalence varies, so the mechanism is certain while frequency is not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: All incoming string chunks and the joined duplicate of a fragmented OSC/DCS/control-string payload
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained memory grows linearly with every server-output chunk until a terminator arrives; completion joins the entire retained payload into another large string. Continuous chunks also reset the prediction timeout, so neither size nor lifetime is bounded.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded renderer memory growth followed by a large allocation/parse stall, with terminal output withheld throughout the transfer.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A control-string chunk that did not match the pending prediction caused prediction reconciliation to fail and the chunk was forwarded; later chunks were then streamed with no pending prediction state, so the addon did not retain the full payload.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: When the scanner remains incomplete at offset zero, each new chunk is pushed into _incompleteEscapeChunks and an empty string is returned. _onBeforeProcessData then calls _deferClearingPredictions for every chunk, repeatedly postponing the only timeout that could release the buffer.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1170 newly appends every continuation chunk to `_incompleteEscapeChunks`; this array and scanner-based withholding did not exist before the PR, whose mismatch path rolled back and forwarded output.
Findings.Title: Bound buffering of fragmented control strings
Findings.Impact: If a prediction is pending when a large chunked OSC/DCS payload begins (for example a clipboard or image transfer), all payload bytes are duplicated and held until termination; a long or unterminated transfer can keep growing memory and then stall the UI when join/reconciliation runs.
Findings.Evidence: Lines 1168-1172 append and suppress every continuation while predictions remain. `_onBeforeProcessData` invokes `_deferClearingPredictions` after each server event, and that method disposes/restarts a >=500 ms timeout. The completion path at line 1174 uses `_incompleteEscapeChunks.join('') + complete`, allocating the whole retained payload again. Tests cover only short fragmented strings and do not impose a byte/chunk limit.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not retain arbitrary control-string payloads. Once an incomplete non-CSI control string is detected, roll back/disable pending predictions and immediately forward the buffered/current chunks while keeping only scanner state; alternatively enforce a small byte cap that flushes and exits reconciliation before appending more.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed O(N) copy, retained per-command cell map, and per-character clone call sites are all explicit in the implementation. Exact milliseconds depend on command length and type-ahead activation, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Map entries and short-lived Map allocations on the synchronous terminal input/output path
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a command with N distinct predicted cells, each character adds a cell and both tentative-cursor creation and character confirmation clone the current N-entry map, producing O(N²) entry copies and allocations over the command.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increasing input latency and CPU/GC pressure, potentially freezing local echo for long commands or unbracketed paste bursts on a high-latency terminal.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Cursor.clone copied only cursor coordinates via moveTo, so cloning was O(1) regardless of how many predictions had already been made.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Cursor.clone now calls adopt, and adopt constructs new Map(cursor._cells); the map retains prior predicted cells until prediction state is cleared, while ordinary character handling repeatedly requests tentativeCursor and CharacterPrediction.rollForwards also clones the cursor.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 157 changes adoption from coordinate-only state to `this._cells = new Map(cursor._cells)`, turning every newly added clone/adopt call into a full copy of all accumulated predicted cells; before the diff clone used only `moveTo(this)`.
Findings.Title: Avoid copying all predicted cells on every cursor clone
Findings.Impact: With type-ahead active, a long shell command or plain paste causes progressively larger synchronous copies per key/echo; 1,000 predicted cells entail on the order of a million copied map entries instead of linear work, delaying typing and terminal rendering.
Findings.Evidence: The added cell overlay is populated by CharacterPrediction.apply/setCell. addPrediction invalidates _tenativeCursor after every character, and the ordinary-character path immediately calls tentativeCursor again, whose clone reaches this line. CharacterPrediction.rollForwards also calls cursor.clone for each confirmed character. Confirmed predictions are shifted from _expected but their cells are not removed from Cursor._cells, so the copied map grows across the command until _clearPredictionState clears the cursor.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep cursor cloning O(1), for example with an immutable/shared cell snapshot plus small copy-on-write overlays, or separate coordinate-only clones from the rare operation that truly needs an independent cell map; also discard confirmed cells that can no longer be revisited.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing or pasting a long command while type-ahead is active on a high-latency terminal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The UI-thread terminal onData callback synchronously parses every input character, applies a prediction, recreates the tentative cursor, and writes local echo before input handling can return; cursor-map cloning is therefore directly on the keystroke/render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write predicted and reconciled VT sequences into xterm's parser/render queue
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one predicted write per input event and one rewritten output write per PTY chunk; a multi-character event coalesces the output string but still executes the per-character cursor work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local-echo writes existed, but Cursor.clone copied coordinates in O(1); this diff adds the growing Map copy before those writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Predicted output must be scheduled before local echo is visible, and synchronous preparation delays the input callback and subsequent render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One callback per delivered PTY output chunk; grouping is controlled upstream and unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The addon already reconciled each incoming process-data event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Confirmations drive synchronous reconciliation and then xterm parsing; no new IPC call is issued by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct predicted cells in the current command after effective overwrites; normal forward typing produces N unique coordinates. Each clone copies the accumulated map, yielding O(N²) entry copies over N characters/confirmations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Input callbacks and reconciliation run serially on the renderer event loop. Xterm writes may queue asynchronously, but no worker, limiter, or parallelism moves the Map copies off the synchronous callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cell Map acts as a per-cursor overlay rather than a cache. It retains confirmed coordinates until prediction state clears, clones have no structural sharing, and repeated coordinate reads do not reduce clone cardinality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full Map constructor is explicit, ordinary-character handling invalidates/recreates the tentative cursor per character, roll-forward also clones, and confirmed cells are not removed from the cursor map.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact pause duration depends on command length, local-echo activation, and JS engine Map cost; plain long commands, unbracketed paste, macros, and delayed confirmations establish realistic large N.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium repeated-work regression: O(1) cursor cloning became O(current command length), making the full interaction quadratic and allocation-heavy.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receiving a large or unterminated fragmented OSC/DCS/control string while a prediction remains pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each PTY chunk enters beforeServerInput synchronously. The changed scanner marks the sequence incomplete, appends the chunk, and returns an empty string, so xterm parsing/rendering cannot progress until termination, timeout, cancellation, or disposal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive chunked terminal output from the shell/process host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per upstream output chunk; large clipboard/image/control payloads can produce many chunks. The diff does not add IPC calls but changes every continuation from streamed to retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Incoming PTY events already existed, but a prediction mismatch rolled back and forwarded the first control chunk, after which later chunks streamed normally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The changed return value suppresses every chunk from xterm, blocking parser/render progress until the whole control string is released.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Join all retained control-string chunks into one string and concatenate the completion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One whole-payload allocation when the sequence terminates, after retaining C original chunk strings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No whole-control-string chunk array or final join existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The full join and subsequent reconciliation occur synchronously before completed output can reach xterm.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit released control output to xterm parsing/rendering
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Changed from incremental writes per process chunk to no writes during buffering followed by one potentially very large write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Control output was forwarded incrementally after prediction failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parser/render work is delayed and burst at completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total payload bytes B and chunk count C after the first incomplete sequence. Retention is O(B), the chunks array is O(C), and completion joins/copies O(B); there is no byte or chunk cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PTY callbacks are serialized. Every callback restarts the single prediction-clear timeout, so a continuous transfer prevents cleanup rather than allowing timeout and output processing to overlap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _incompleteEscapeChunks is an unbounded transient buffer, not a cache: there is no deduplication, size cap, spill, or incremental consumption. Completion clears it only after allocating a joined string; cancellation/disposal flushes it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: append-and-suppress, full join, and per-event timeout restart are explicit and reachable whenever a prediction precedes a fragmented control string.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency and payload size vary by terminal workload, but OSC clipboard/image transfers can be large and an unterminated stream establishes no finite upper bound.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high unbounded-retention regression: the addon can duplicate and indefinitely retain an arbitrary process-output payload while blocking terminal progress.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fish and PSReadLine repaint reconciliation after each edit
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each incoming repaint is scanned, parsed into row cells, compared against pending predictions, and pending edits are reapplied before the rewritten output reaches xterm.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one or several chunks per keypress, controlled by shell and transport fragmentation; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same PTY output arrived, but unsupported repaint patterns caused prediction rollback rather than detailed row reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reconciliation is synchronous before forwarding to xterm, but it avoids extra subprocess/network calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write reconciled repaint VT data to xterm
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One rewritten write per incoming chunk, with fragmented sequences sometimes withheld and coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Output was also passed to xterm after simpler matching/rollback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Visible repaint waits for synchronous row parsing and prediction reapplication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the current terminal row width W cells and P pending predictions. Erase-to-end and reapply paths can approach O(W*P), but normal per-key shell replies keep P small and W is bounded by terminal columns.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized per PTY output event on the renderer event loop; there is no parallel work or external limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cell snapshots are temporary per repaint and discarded after the callback. Cursor overlays persist for prediction reconciliation; no cold/warm external cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous O(W*P) code shape; lower for harmful magnitude under realistic effective P.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very wide terminals and unusual bursts increase W and P, but repository tests and shell behavior show ordinary repaint confirmations quickly reduce P; no independent high-confidence user-visible regression beyond the reported cursor-copy mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: added repaint support performs bounded row-local work, and realistic effective cardinality did not prove a separate actionable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resizing, title changes, configuration changes, and latency-stat updates reevaluate whether predictions are shown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Events schedule a RunOnceScheduler for 100 ms; only the last pending reevaluation executes, and no external operation must complete before the event handler returns.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Event frequency during resize/config/title/stat bursts; effective execution count is coalesced to one per quiet 100 ms window.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single serialized scheduler; repeated schedule calls coalesce rather than fan out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No external cache. Predictor statistics and configuration values are in-memory; scheduler disposal is registered with addon lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from direct scheduler construction and schedule call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the changed scheduler preserves debounce-like coalescing and improves explicit cleanup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: repeated reevaluation remains coalesced and scheduled work is lifecycle-owned.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. Submitted two diff-caused findings: quadratic cursor-cell Map copying on interactive input/reconciliation and unbounded buffering of fragmented control strings. Repaint, scheduling, timer cleanup, marker lifecycle, style serialization, tests, and all changed/transitive boundaries were inspected; no concrete PR-fixed shipped regression warranted blame/report_regression_fix.
